question: On 23 February 2024, Euronews published the article ‘Fraud office handling complaints over jobs at European trade mark agency’. The article explains that the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) has received two complaints alleging irregularities in recruitment at the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) based in Alicante.

The article states that the complaints lodged last year involve various appointments and allege irregularities in the pre-selection process and partiality, nepotism and corruption in a number of recruitment and selection procedures. The complaints claim that irregularities often occur in the preselection committees’ work so as to submit single candidates for selection or favour specific candidates.
What is more, according to Euronews, local municipal authorities in Alicante were involved in two of the recruitment processes for which complaints were lodged. 1.

Can the Commission confirm that OLAF has received the reports mentioned in the article and that EUIPO is being investigated for irregular recruitment and that Alicante’s municipal authorities are affected by that investigation?
Can the Commission confirm that the investigation involves Alicante Municipal Council or positions or people who have professional or personal connections to it?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2024) The European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) is independent in the exercise of its mandate. OLAF does not usually issue comments on cases it may or may not be treating. This is in order to protect the confidentiality of any possible investigations and of possible ensuing judicial proceedings, as well as to ensure respect for personal data and procedural rights.
